strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit`/`offset` (limit capped at MAX_LIMIT=50, default DEFAULT_LIMIT=20), returns `{ total, items }`, and rejects non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Tests start the real app in-process on an OS-chosen port (as the existing suite does) and assert against the real catalogue imported from src/catalogue.js.
inScope: Search by q (case-insensitive substring of name)
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
The shop's search box UI (not in this repository)
assumptions: The real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0; nothing is faked. Expected data is derived from the exported PRODUCTS, DEFAULT_LIMIT and MAX_LIMIT, so it follows the catalogue.
Results are in catalogue order (the handler filters PRODUCTS without sorting), so page contents can be asserted exactly.
`total` is the count of all matches, independent of limit/offset.
Negative numbers (e.g. offset=-1) count as not a whole number and get 400, as the handler's /^\d+$/ check does.
openQuestions: The ticket doesn't say what the cap is or the default page size; tests use the app's MAX_LIMIT (50) and DEFAULT_LIMIT (20).
Is an empty `limit=` meant to be a 400 (current behaviour) or treated as absent?

risks.description: Search is case-sensitive or matches on other fields, so shoppers miss products
risks.mitigation: TC1 searches with mixed/upper case and asserts the exact set of matching ids

risks.description: total reflects the page length instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC3/TC4 assert total stays the full match count while items are a slice

risks.description: Uncapped limit lets clients pull the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts a huge limit returns exactly MAX_LIMIT items

risks.description: Bad paging params produce 500s or silently wrong pages
risks.mitigation: TC6–TC8 assert 400 for each invalid form

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns only products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without `q` every product is matched.
Results are paged by `limit` and `offset`, the response includes `total` (number of all matches), and limits above the maximum are capped.
A non-whole-number `limit` or `offset`, or a `limit` below 1, gets 400.

testCases.title: matches q against product names regardless of case
preconditions: App listening on an ephemeral port
testCases.expected: 200; total and item ids equal exactly the PRODUCTS whose lowercased name contains 'tea' (Teapot, Tea strainer), in catalogue order

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products

testCases.title: returns the page at offset with limit items and the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total = number of Kettle products (15); item ids = matches[3..7)
testCases.rationale: Paging combined with search and total

testCases.title: returns no items but the full total when offset is past the last match
caps a limit above the maximum
testCases.expected: 200; exactly MAX_LIMIT (50) items, the first 50 products; total 120

testCases.title: refuses a limit or offset that is not a whole number with 400
steps: GET /products with each of limit=abc, limit=2.5, offset=abc, offset=1.5, offset=-1
testCases.expected: Each responds 400 (test.each, one case per value)

testCases.title: accepts limit 1 and offset 0 as the smallest valid page
testCases.rationale: Valid side of the limit boundary

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. The real app is started in-process with createApp().listen(0) per test file and closed afterwards. Runs under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).
